newsitem.title: UK: UK unemployment falling at trend level - minister.
newsitem.headline: UK unemployment falling at trend level - minister.

text.p: The trend in unemployment is firmly downwards, in line with the past few months, although October's large drop may have been exaggerated by a new jobless benefits system, UK employment minister Eric Forth said on Wednesday.

"We feel this figure is somewhat overstated because of the transition to the jobseekers allowance system that we implemented just a month ago," Forth said on Reuters Financial Television. "But the underlying fall is very much in line with the last few months and we're still talking about a 15-20,000 per month fall. We're on trend for that."
The job seekers allowance replaced unemployment benefit on October 6 and demands more from claimants in terms of actively seeking work.
Forth said the 40,800 fall in unemployment in October was quite likely either to be revised or to be followed by a bounceback next month. But the trend was firmly down, he said.
Looking at wage costs and earnings, Forth said the picture was "one of steady growth without anything being in a threatening position."
He said all the evidence suggested that the rate at which unemployment in Britain becomes inflationary, had come down.
"It may be we're genuinely entering a new phase now where the relationships between some of these factors...are coming into question. We don't necessarily see inflation pressures appearing."
He noted that U.S. unemployment had stuck below six percent for a considerable period of time but inflation and interest rates remain low.
Forth said he saw no reason for the recent quarter-point rise in official UK interest rates, taking them to six percent, to affect the trend in unemployment.
